We need to add support for a json data editor, similar like we have the markdown editor.

* This should be a stand alone component
* when the user clicks on a link that is a json file, the editor should be opened
  * when in card-view, this should be a popup, similar like the card or action popups, so managed by the [card_popup_service.ts](app/src/services/card_popup_service.ts)
  * when in list view, this should be a new tab with a data editor
* for an array, show a table, the columns are the field names of the objects inside the array, if the array has primitives, there is only 1 column, 'values'	
  * user can add & delete, copy, cut, paste records.
  * user can select multiple records for copy, cut or delete
  * fields allow for inline editing
* for objects, show a form, with fields layout out vertically
* if a field value is a list or object, show a button to dig into the value. this is for objects and for lists. 
  * at the top of the data editor is a breadcrumb component that displays the path into the data.
    * user can click on items to go back

## Current state

`MarkdownEditor` renders repository links, but no application route opens project JSON data. List-view tabs support only cards, actions, and agent instruction Markdown. Repository JSON paths may appear in the file-tree folder structure, but arbitrary JSON files are not open documents and cannot be edited there.

`CardPopupService` owns action, card-details, and card-sequence popups. It has no JSON popup entry. Existing storage bridges can list repository paths, load a text file, and write files, but `ProjectPersistenceService` saves only open card, action, and instruction drafts.

## implementation details

* Add a stan

re` and only render or invoke service operations.
* Intercept clicks on project-local links whose path ends in `.json`, resolving relative paths from the Markdown document containing the link. Keep HTTP, HTTPS, anchor, non-JSON, and paths outside the active project on their current link path.
* In card view, add a `json-data` entry to `CardPopupService` and render the editor in the shared popup stack. In list view, extend `OpenFilesService`, `TabBar`, `TextEditorPane`, and project persistence with a JSON document kind so one tab exists per resolved project-relative path.
* Load JSON through the active storage text-file API. Parse before exposing editable data. Show malformed, missing, and unreadable-file errors through `dialogService`; do not create or mutate editor state during render.
* Save valid JSON through the existing project persistence flow, using stable pretty-printed JSON and a final newline. Read-only projects render data but disable every mutation. If storage reports an external change while the document is dirty, keep the draft and warn instead of overwriting it.
* Render an object as vertically stacked property-name/value rows. Strings, numbers, booleans, and `null` use type-preserving inline controls; property names are not editable in this feature. A root primitive uses the same single-value control.
* Render an array containing only objects as a table whose columns are the union of object field names in first-seen order. Render every other array, including empty and mixed-type arrays, with one `values` column. Missing object fields display an empty cell and remain missing until edited.
* Array selection supports one or many rows. Add inserts an empty object for an object table and `null` for a `values` table. Delete removes selected rows. Copy writes selected values, in row order, as a JSON array. Cut removes rows only after clipboard writing succeeds. Paste accepts a JSON array and inserts its values after the last selected row, or at the end when nothing is selected; invalid clipboard JSON leaves data unchanged and shows an error.
* Replace nested object or array values with a drill-in button. Breadcrumb starts at the file root and adds one item for each property name or array index traversed. Clicking an ancestor item returns to that exact value; edits that remove the current value return the editor to its closest existing ancestor.
* Add focused service and component tests for link routing by workspace view, popup/tab reuse, loading and save failures, object and array layouts, mixed and empty arrays, scalar editing, row operations, clipboard failure, breadcrumbs, read-only behavior, and dirty external changes.

## acceptance criteria

* Clicking a project-local `.json` link in card view opens one managed JSON popup anchored to the clicked link; clicking the same link again activates the existing popup.
* Clicking a project-local `.json` link in list view opens or activates one JSON tab for that resolved path.
* External, anchor, and non-JSON links retain current behavior. Missing, unreadable, or malformed JSON shows a clear error and does not open an editable document.
* Objects display vertical fields. Object-only arrays display a table with the union of their field names. Primitive, mixed, and empty arrays display one `values` column. Root primitive values remain editable.
* Nested objects and arrays open through a drill-in control. Breadcrumb shows each traversed property or index and lets user return to any ancestor.
* User can edit scalar values without changing their JSON type. Array add, multi-row selection, delete, copy, cut, and paste preserve row order and produce valid JSON.
* Invalid edits or clipboard content never change draft data. Failed clipboard writes never remove cut rows.
* Saving writes stable pretty-printed JSON through existing project persistence. Read-only projects cannot change data, and dirty drafts are not overwritten by external file changes.
* JSON popup and tab state survives unrelated React rerenders and closes through existing popup and tab controls.

- `MarkdownEditor` treats JSON links as ordinary browser links. In the packaged app, a relative path resolves against the bundled `index.html`, producing a `file://` navigation.
- `file://` pages have origin `null`. The desktop preload correctly rejects that untrusted location and replaces the page with `MD² desktop bridges blocked for origin: null`.
- The security check is not the defect and should not be weakened. The missing behavior is application-level routing for project JSON links.
- The unfinished `F_467_json_data_editor` worktree already implements the intended approach: preserve the original Markdown URL, intercept project-local `.json` clicks before browser navigation, resolve them relative to the Markdown document, and open the JSON popup or tab.

Proposed solution: finish and integrate F_467’s JSON-link interception. Add focused tests proving relative JSON links are intercepted while HTTP, anchor, non-JSON, and out-of-project links retain their existing behavior.

> The security check is not the defect and should not be weakened.

it should definitely be improved cause now it is an application failure: the user is no longer able to recover from this error

so we should fix this bit for other data types that might fail in a similar way. 

f-467 will take care of the json files

You are right. F-467 fixes JSON routing, but the desktop shell must independently prevent an unsupported link from replacing the application and provide recovery if prevention fails. I’ll refine that cross-file-type safeguard.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

+## Current state
+
+Markdown links use normal browser navigation. In the packaged desktop application, a relative file link can resolve to a `file://` location and replace the trusted renderer document.
+
+The preload script then runs in the new renderer document. Because a local file has origin `null` and does not match the trusted application location, the preload correctly withholds all desktop bridges and replaces the document body with `MD² desktop bridges blocked for origin: null`. The user is left on that page and cannot return to the running application.
+
+`registerNavigationGuards` in `desktop/src/shell/renderer_security.js` is intended to prevent this. It currently handles `will-navigate` through the deprecated positional URL argument and denies new windows through `setWindowOpenHandler`, but the failing navigation path still reaches the untrusted document. JSON-specific application routing belongs to F-467; this bug must prevent the same application failure for every unsupported link type.
+
+## implementation details
+
+* Update `registerNavigationGuards` to inspect Electron's current navigation-event details and prevent untrusted main-frame navigation before it commits. Use `will-frame-navigate` and its `url` and `isMainFrame` fields instead of the deprecated positional `will-navigate` arguments.
+* Allow navigation only to the exact trusted renderer document. Continue ignoring its hash when comparing locations so in-application hash navigation remains valid.
+* For HTTP and HTTPS destinations, prevent application navigation and open the URL through `shell.openExternal`, as today.
+* For every other untrusted destination, including `file://`, prevent navigation without loading that document. Do not relax the preload origin check and do not recover by reloading the application after navigation.
+* Keep `setWindowOpenHandler` as the new-window guard with the same protocol policy.
+* Update `renderer_security.test.mjs` to invoke the handlers with Electron's current event shape. Cover trusted application navigation, HTTP and HTTPS external links, local files, unsupported protocols, main-frame navigation, and subframe navigation.
+* `registerNavigationGuards` has one production call site in `desktop/main.js`; update it directly without a compatibility flag or alternate mode.
+
+## acceptance criteria
+
+* Clicking a local or otherwise unsupported link cannot replace the MD² renderer document.
+* After a blocked navigation, the current application view and unsaved renderer state remain intact.
+* HTTP and HTTPS links open in the operating system's external browser and do not navigate the MD² window.
+* New-window requests follow the same protocol restrictions as same-window navigation.
+* The trusted renderer document remains loadable, including its in-application hash changes.
+* The preload continues to expose no desktop bridges when an untrusted document is loaded directly.
+* JSON-specific link handling is unchanged by this bug fix and remains owned by F-467.

when clicking on a link in the markdown editor pointing to a json file, we now get a white screen with a text: `md2 desktop bridges blocked for origin: null`

this was not the case with the previous build, so the last couple of cards must of broken something.

## Current state

Markdown links use normal browser navigation. In the packaged desktop application, a relative file link can resolve to a `file://` location and replace the trusted renderer document.

The preload script then runs in the new renderer document. Because a local file has origin `null` and does not match the trusted application location, the preload correctly withholds all desktop bridges and replaces the document body with `MDÂ² desktop bridges blocked for origin: null`. The user is left on that page and cannot return to the running application.

`registerNavigationGuards` in `desktop/src/shell/renderer_security.js` is intended to prevent this. It currently handles `will-navigate` through the deprecated positional URL argument and denies new windows through `setWindowOpenHandler`, but the failing navigation path still reaches the untrusted document. JSON-specific application routing belongs to F-467; this bug must prevent the same application failure for every unsupported link type.

## implementation details

* Update `registerNavigationGuards` to inspect Electron's current navigation-event details and prevent untrusted main-frame navigation before it commits. Use `will-frame-navigate` and its `url` and `isMainFrame` fields instead of the deprecated positional `will-navigate` arguments.
* Allow navigation only to the exact trusted renderer document. Continue ignoring its hash when comparing locations so in-application hash navigation remains valid.
* For HTTP and HTTPS destinations, prevent application navigation and open the URL through `shell.openExternal`, as today.
* For every other untrusted destination, including `file://`, prevent navigation without loading that document. Do not relax the preload origin check and do not recover by reloading the application after navigation.
* Keep `setWindowOpenHandler` as the new-window guard with the same protocol policy.
* Update `renderer_security.test.mjs` to invoke the handlers with Electron's current event shape. Cover trusted application navigation, HTTP and HTTPS external links, local files, unsupported protocols, main-frame navigation, and subframe navigation.
* `registerNavigationGuards` has one production call site in `desktop/main.js`; update it directly without a compatibility flag or alternate mode.

## acceptance criteria

* Clicking a local or otherwise unsupported link cannot replace the MDÂ² renderer document.
* After a blocked navigation, the current application view and unsaved renderer state remain intact.
* HTTP and HTTPS links open in the operating system's external browser and do not navigate the MDÂ² window.
* New-window requests follow the same protocol restrictions as same-window navigation.
* The trusted renderer document remains loadable, including its in-application hash changes.
* The preload continues to expose no desktop bridges when an untrusted document is loaded directly.
* JSON-specific link handling is unchanged by this bug fix and remains owned by F-467.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |
